accepted_content.description:
What can be sent to the channel, and how much. Empty for channels that
can't be written to, such as a voice channel without text chat.

members.description:
The ids of the users in the channel, or `None` when it is open to its
whole organization or the platform doesn't say.

parent.description:
The channel this one is in, such as a thread's channel or a channel's
category.

position.description: Where the channel sorts among its siblings, lowest first.

oneOf.description: Only some users can post, such as a news channel.
Holds threads rather than messages.
A conversation branched off another channel, its parent.
Groups other channels, which name it as their parent.
A conversation between two users.
A conversation between a few users, outside any channel list.
Anything else the platform has, named by the provider.

ChannelRef.description:
Where a channel is: in an organization, or in the provider's standalone
scope when `organization` is `None`.

CommandError.description: Why a provider couldn't carry out a [`Command`].

oneOf.description: The provider or platform can't do this.
Invalid function arguments, with codes and messages for each input.

A platform-specific failure with a stable code and optional data,
such as confirmed progress after a partial failure. A details record with
`delivery_unknown: false` confirms that an action did not take effect;
the app API otherwise treats these action errors as uncertain.
The content breaks the channel's rules or limits.

Too many requests; try again after this many milliseconds, if the
platform says.
The account isn't allowed to, such as post in an announcement channel.
The account must log in first; see [`ProviderStatus::LoginRequired`].
The orchestrator cancelled the command before it was carried out.
Anything else, as the provider describes it.
Text with styles and mentions. Counts toward the text limit.

Anything else the platform has, such as a sticker or a poll, in a
format the provider defines.

ContentKind.description: The kinds of [`Content`], used to say what a [`Channel`] accepts.

oneOf.description: Matches [`Content::Custom`] with the same `kind`.

ContentRule.description:
What a channel takes of one kind of content.

A channel can have several rules for a kind, such as small WebP stickers
and larger images of any type. A part follows the first rule for its kind
that takes its MIME type.

max_size.description:
For text, the longest all of a message's text parts can be together,
formatted or not, counted in [`ContentRule::text_unit`]s. Formatted
text follows the text rule's limit; its own `max_size` is unused. For anything else, the most
bytes in each part.

mime_types.description:
The MIME types taken for media, such as `image/png`, or `image/*` for
any image. Empty takes any.

DirectoryUpdate.description:
A change to the organizations, users and channels a provider is part of.

Upserts add the item, or replace the one with the same id. Removals of
items that aren't there are not an error for the provider.

oneOf.description: Adds an organization, or replaces it along with its users and channels.
Changes an organization's details, keeping its users and channels.
The account left the organization, or it was deleted.

Sets the account's own user id in a scope, or clears it with `None`.
Removing that user clears it too.

Whether a user is around. Users can have a presence before they are
reported, such as in large organizations.

Forgets everything the provider reported, such as before a full
snapshot after reconnecting.

Email.description: Mail envelope and state. Thread references use RFC Message-IDs, not channel-local ids.

content_ids.description: MIME Content-IDs by content index, for inline images in HTML.

html.description: Alternative to the plain text body in content. Never render without sanitizing.

EmailAddress.description: An RFC mailbox address, with an optional display name.

FormattedText.description: Text with styled ranges. Ranges can nest and overlap.

text.description:
The text as it reads without formatting, including a mention's
display text, such as `@Ana`.

input.description: `None` means the issue applies to the whole input set.

LoginStep.description:
One step of logging in. Show the message along with whatever else the
step has.

function.description:
An [`ActionKind::Login`] function in the provider context to fill in
and call, such as with a password or a code. The provider reports the
next status before answering it.

link.description: A page to open in a browser, such as an OAuth login.

message.description: What to tell the user, such as "Enter the code we texted you".

qr_code.description:
Text to show as a QR code for the platform's phone app to scan.
Reported again when it changes.

Mailbox.description: A mail folder. Attributes retain server special-use flags such as \Sent.

mime.description: The MIME type, such as `image/png`, if known.

name.description: The file name, if the platform has one.

size.description: The size in bytes, if known. Ignored for [`MediaSource::Bytes`].

MediaMetadata.description: Hints for displaying media. Unknown values stay absent; URLs can expire.

oneOf.description: The file itself. The whole message must fit in [`MAX_FRAME`].
Where the file can be downloaded without credentials.

A file held by the side that sent the message: the provider in the
messages it emits, the orchestrator in its commands. The other side
reads it in pieces, so it can be any size. Use it too for files only
the provider can download, such as ones behind the platform's login.

A provider's blob stays readable until the orchestrator sends
[`Command::ReleaseBlob`]. Each id belongs to the one event or reply
it came in: a provider that returns the same file again, such as in
history, gives it a new id, so releasing one never takes the file from
another reader. At most [`MAX_ID`] bytes.

Mention.description: Who or what a mention points at. Ids are in the channel's scope.

oneOf.description: A group of users the platform names, such as a Discord role.
Everyone in the channel, such as `@everyone` or `@channel`.

author.description: The author's [`User`] id, in the channel's scope.

content.description: The parts of the message, in order, such as a caption and its image.

edited_at.description: When it was last edited, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

email.description: Mail fields; absent for chat messages. HTML is untrusted and must be sanitized by clients.

nonce.description:
The client's id for a message the account sent through
[`Command::Send`], when the provider can tell which send it is. It
settles a send whose answer never came.

reply_to.description: The id of the message this replies to, in the same channel.

sent_at.description: When it was sent, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

MessageEvent.description:
Something that happened to a message or in a channel.

Events can repeat, such as when history overlaps live messages or a
provider replays what it missed. Clients keep messages by channel and id:
a [`MessageEvent::Received`] for a known id replaces it.

oneOf.description: A new message, including ones the account sent itself.

edited_at.description: In milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

oneOf.description: A user added or removed a reaction.

`user`, which can be the account, has read the channel up to and
including `up_to`, or nothing in it when `None`.

`user` is typing. It lasts until they send a message, or for
[`TYPING_TIMEOUT_MS`] unless repeated.

The provider may have missed events in this channel and can't replay
them, such as after a reconnect. Load its history again.

A [`Command::Send`] with this nonce never reached the platform, so it
is safe to send again. Without this or a [`Message`] carrying the
nonce, delivery is unknown.

max_attachments.description: The most media and custom parts in one message.

max_total_size.description: The most bytes of media and custom parts in one message, together.

Organization.description: A group on a platform, such as a Discord server or a Slack workspace.

me.description: The account's own user id in the organization, if it has one.

users.description:
Can be partial, such as when the platform sends large member lists in
chunks; send the rest with [`DirectoryUpdate::UserUpserted`].

oneOf.description: Do not disturb.

ProviderId.description:
Identifies one spawn, even when providers reuse a name or their events
come from different orchestrators in this process. Not a persistent id.

instance.description: Unique across spawns in this process.

name.description: The configured name, also used for persistent secrets.

ProviderStatus.description:
Where a provider is in connecting to its platform. Reported with
[`ProviderMessage::Status`]; a provider starts as `Connecting`.

A provider reports `Syncing` before its directory snapshot, then `Ready`
once it has sent it, along with replays or [`MessageEvent::Gap`]s for
what it missed. Commands sent before `Ready` can fail, such as with
[`CommandError::LoginRequired`].

oneOf.description:
The account must log in; the step says how. Reported again for each
following step.
The connection was lost, and the provider is trying again.
The provider can't go on without help, such as for a banned account.

Reaction.description: The reactions to a message with one key.

key.description: A Unicode emoji such as `👍`, or the provider's id for a custom one.

me.description: Whether the account is one of them.

Span.description: A style over `text[start..end]`, in UTF-8 bytes.

oneOf.description: Unicode scalar values, Rust's `char`s.
UTF-16 code units, as JavaScript counts string length.
UTF-8 bytes.

Value.description: Files can use blobs inside `Content`. Custom records need no new variants.

Violation.description: How a message breaks a channel's rules. Parts are numbered from 0.

oneOf.description: The message has no content.
The channel doesn't take the part's kind of content.

The channel doesn't take the part's MIME type, or needs one and the
part has none.
`length` is in the rule's [`TextUnit`].
A formatted part has a span outside its text.

description:
Something a provider instance did. `Exited` is its last event. There is
no ordering between instances, including ones that reuse a name.

oneOf.description:
A change to the organizations, users and channels the provider is part
of.

Where the provider is in connecting to its platform, such as needing
a login.
